wins.text: Firm reported net income of $14.6B, EPS of $5.07 on revenue of $46B with ROTCE of 21%, up 8% YoY
Markets revenue up 21% YoY to record performance; Equities up 48% YoY on elevated volatility and strong derivatives monetization
IB fees up 12% YoY with #1 wallet share at 9%; Advisory up 16%, Debt underwriting up 16%
AWM AUM reached $4.1T and client assets $6T, both up 15% YoY; long-term net inflows of $54B in the quarter
Firm distributed $11B of capital to shareholders including $7.1B of net common share repurchases; CET1 ratio of 15.4% with $30B-$60B of estimated excess capital

risks.text: Reserve build of $973M driven by increased probability weightings on downside scenarios; weighted average unemployment embedded in allowance raised to 5.8% from 5.5%, reflecting significantly elevated macro uncertainty
JPMorgan economist puts recession probability at ~50/50; Jamie Dimon expects S&P earnings estimates to move from +5% to 0% or negative, with many companies likely to pull guidance
IB pipeline conversion at risk as corporate clients shift to wait-and-see mode on tariff uncertainty; equity underwriting fees already down 9% YoY on challenging market conditions
NII ex Markets faces headwind from rate curve now pricing ~3 cuts vs. 1 cut previously; lower front-end rates mechanically pressure asset-sensitive balance sheet
Geopolitical and trade war risk could put JPMorgan in the crosshairs internationally; Jamie Dimon acknowledged some clients or countries may feel differently about American banks

guidance_items.detail: NII ex Markets maintained at ~$90B; firm-wide NII outlook increased slightly to ~$94.5B reflecting higher Markets NII, largely offset in NIR
Card net charge-off rate guidance maintained at ~3.6%, though Jamie Dimon cautioned this is highly uncertain given wide range of macro outcomes

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential for private credit / non-bank lenders to re-intermediate back to traditional banks amid volatility — not proactively addressed
Treasury market functioning and potential Fed intervention (QT pause, treasury purchases) amid 10-year yield spike — not mentioned in prepared remarks
Cost optimization / expense war room efforts and internal efficiency initiatives — not disclosed proactively by management
